dimension_justifications.soundness: The paper narrowly states its claims and describes strong relational checks, selected independent numerical oracles, matched fault controls, and explicit memory denominators. However, the PDF contains an unresolved provenance ambiguity between declaring frozen identity fully witnessed and reporting that terminal recursive code closure failed. The central semantic evidence also remains a mixture of common-path exactness and sampled operator-level oracles rather than an independent end-to-end validation.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The nine-page main text is logically ordered, and the abstract, introduction, results, limitations, and conclusion are quantitatively consistent. Nevertheless, heavy artifact-internal vocabulary, late clarification of overloaded terms such as exact, repeated boundary disclaimers, small figure labels, dense appendix tables, and truncated line numbers materially increase the effort needed to reconstruct the experiment and audit logic.
dimension_justifications.contribution: An executable, phase-aware ownership audit for heterogeneous KV and recurrent state is potentially useful, and the paper distinguishes this integration from prior caching policies. Its demonstrated scope is nevertheless one positive model/runtime/adapter case, with the different-runtime cohort yielding only a negative boundary result. The resulting generalizable knowledge is currently narrow for ICLR and does not establish a new serving mechanism, portable standard, scheduler property, or production capability.

paper_summary: The paper proposes FORKAUDIT, a seven-target executable contract for auditing document-prefix sharing and request-state isolation in hybrid LLMs containing paged attention KV and recurrent GDN state. A four-cell factorial varies full-copy versus shared-document KV and materialized versus borrowed GDN bases for one Qwen3.5-35B-A3B/vLLM case. Reported evidence includes cross-cell and cross-fan-out equality, pointer-free storage witnesses, selected dense-FP32 attention and NumPy GDN checks, nine live fault injections, lifecycle controls, and separated allocator denominators. The paper explicitly limits its conclusions to one positive runtime, one hardware family, and a sequential schedule.
strongest_verified_contribution: Within the PDF, the strongest contribution is the concrete phase-aware ownership contract that separates immutable document state, private append state, borrowed recurrent bases, first-transition rebinding, dispatch receipts, and memory denominators, together with a mutation-tested reference case whose headline counts and numerical values remain consistent across the abstract, results, limitations, and conclusion.
strengths: The paper consistently avoids converting allocator deltas into unsupported throughput, scheduler-capacity, or process-memory claims.
The abstract, Introduction, Sections 5–6, and Conclusion agree on the main counts, numerical results, negative runtime-transfer result, and scope limitations.
The seven audit targets and the full/partial/open decision language provide a useful structure for separating witnessed properties from untested properties.
Matched-clean fault controls and explicit wrong-gate and escaped-fault categories are more informative than merely stating that assertions exist.
The main text occupies exactly nine pages, followed by references and clearly labeled appendices, and includes a reproducibility statement before the references.
questions: How can Table 5 classify frozen identity as fully witnessed when Section 7 states that terminal recursive code closure failed and the derivative binds a new package manifest rather than a closed original run identifier?

Does runtime-independent in Section 3 mean only that the record schema is runtime-agnostic, or that the decision rule has been empirically validated across runtimes? Could the paper state this distinction at the first use?

Can the authors provide one compact main-text matrix mapping every cohort to its factor axes, sampling unit, supported claim, and excluded claim, so that RR2, rank, window, cell, shard, phase artifact, and sidecar need not be reconstructed across the main text and appendix?

Can exact be qualified at first use as token equality, canonical CPU-FP32 byte-digest equality, logical-state digest equality, or tolerance-based oracle agreement, rather than relying on the definition introduced later on page 4?
Are the displayed line-number truncations after 954 and 1054 intentional? If not, can they be corrected so review references remain unique?

issues.location: Abstract, page 1, lines 11–34; Introduction, pages 1–2, lines 53–107; Sections 4.1–4.3, pages 5–6; Section 5, pages 7–9; Appendix Table 4, page 14
issues.observed_evidence: The main narrative introduces many operational units and artifact terms—rank, window, cell, RR2, shard, sidecar, phase artifact, registered observable, fixed-axis projection, and gate—across several sections. The definitive cohort-to-claim map appears only in Appendix Table 4. The abstract consequently presents numerous counts and digest types before the reader has a compact model of the execution units and evidence hierarchy.
issues.why_it_matters: The reader must reverse-engineer which observations belong to the primary factorial, earlier capacity cohort, lifecycle cohort, GDN oracle, or runtime-transfer negative before evaluating the claims. This obscures an otherwise careful experimental design and makes accidental cross-cohort interpretation more likely.
issues.required_fix: Add a compact main-text design-and-evidence table immediately before the protocol or results. For each cohort, list the factor axes, N values, sampling unit, number of configurations, primary predicate, authorized claim, and principal exclusion. Define the operational vocabulary there, remove RR2 and other package-internal labels from reader-facing prose unless indispensable, and simplify the abstract to the problem, contract, strongest validation outcomes, and scope.
issues.verification_test: Give the revised first six pages to a technically qualified reader without the appendix and ask them to identify the four factorial cells, the meaning of one configuration and one rank, which cohort supports each headline result, and which cohorts are not pooled. All answers should be recoverable from one main-text table and definitions preceding first use.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is needed; the existing cohort descriptions and Appendix Table 4 are sufficient.

issues.location: Section 3, page 4, lines 178–209; Section 7, page 9, lines 466–476; Appendix Table 5, page 14, lines 731–747; Appendix Table 14, page 20, lines 1035–1054
issues.observed_evidence: Target 1 requires frozen code identity, and Table 5 marks Frozen identity as full. Section 7 nevertheless says that the primary GPU aggregate's terminal recursive code closure failed on post-ledger pycache files and that the derivative uses a new package manifest rather than a closed original run identifier. The PDF does not enumerate the uncovered files or explain why they cannot affect executed semantics.
issues.why_it_matters: Frozen identity is a normative target and underpins the claim that ownership and semantic receipts correspond to one fixed execution. Without an explicit reconciliation, readers cannot determine whether this is harmless generated-file noise or a gap in the provenance chain.
issues.required_fix: Reconcile the status directly in Section 7 and Table 5. Enumerate the files excluded from terminal closure, state whether any could contain or load executable code, identify the pre-execution hashes covering imported source, and either demonstrate complete semantic source coverage or downgrade Frozen identity to partial. Make Table 14 point to the precise closure receipt rather than only a directory.
issues.verification_test: A blind replay should map every source module imported by the primary run to a pre-execution digest and show that every file omitted by terminal recursive closure is generated, non-imported, and semantically irrelevant. Otherwise the target status must be partial everywhere.
issues.evidence_needed: The exact pre-execution source manifest, import/module inventory, omitted-file list, and replay output connecting those records to the primary aggregate.

issues.location: Introduction, page 2, lines 79–107; Section 3, page 4, lines 198–209; Section 5.3, page 8, lines 409–418; Discussion, page 9, lines 448–464; Conclusion, page 9, lines 478–485
issues.observed_evidence: The paper calls the decision rule runtime-independent, but all positive empirical evidence uses one Qwen3.5/vLLM adapter and one hardware family. The Transformers DynamicCache cohort fails the clean dense semantic oracle on all eight ranks and therefore supplies only negative boundary evidence. Later qualifications are responsible, but the distinction between a runtime-agnostic record specification and empirically demonstrated portability is not made at the first claim.
issues.why_it_matters: The generality of the audit contract is central to its contribution. Ambiguous use of runtime-independent can make a schema-level design property sound like a validated transfer result, while the current evidence ceiling is explicitly one positive adapter.
issues.required_fix: Replace runtime-independent with runtime-agnostic interface specification unless portability is directly demonstrated. At first use, separate three claims: the abstract record schema does not name a runtime, one adapter instantiates it successfully, and transfer to another runtime is not established. Use the same three-part boundary in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.
issues.verification_test: Search the revised paper for runtime-independent, portable, general, and transfer. Every occurrence should identify whether it concerns schema syntax, one-adapter evidence, or empirical cross-runtime validation, with no positive portability implication unsupported by the negative cohort.
issues.evidence_needed: No new evidence is needed for accurate claim narrowing. A clean independent runtime or second hybrid model would be needed to elevate the portability claim.

issues.location: Abstract, page 1, lines 17–25; Introduction contribution bullets, page 2, lines 92–101; exactness definition, page 4, lines 211–213; Sections 5.1–5.3, pages 7–8
issues.observed_evidence: The paper uses exact for tokens, canonical CPU-FP32 logit bytes, logical-KV digests, GDN digests, and cross-cell equality, while attention and recurrent oracle results are tolerance-based. The canonicalization qualification appears only on page 4, after exact-match language in the abstract and contribution list.
issues.why_it_matters: These are materially different equivalence notions. Delayed qualification makes it easy to misread exact as device-side bitwise equivalence or as independent end-to-end semantic validation.
issues.required_fix: Introduce a short equivalence vocabulary before the first numerical claim: token exactness, canonical-byte equality, logical-state digest equality, and tolerance-based numerical agreement. Use these terms consistently in the abstract, Figure 3, results, and conclusion.
issues.verification_test: For every use of exact or match, the revised sentence or immediately preceding definition should identify the compared observable, serialization boundary, and whether the criterion is equality or a numerical tolerance.

issues.location: Figures 1–2, pages 2 and 5; Appendix Tables 4–5, pages 14–15; Tables 9–10, pages 17–18; Table 14, page 20; line-number margins on pages 14, 18, and 20
issues.observed_evidence: Several labels in Figures 1–2 and the appendix tables are small at normal page scale, with aggressive hyphenation and long paths reducing scanability. Table 10 is especially compressed. Margin line numbers lose leading digits after 954 and 1054, producing labels such as 55 and 055 that duplicate earlier line numbers.
issues.why_it_matters: The figures and tables are intended to make the audit auditable, but small text and ambiguous line locators impede reading, citation, and verification.
issues.required_fix: Increase figure label size, split the densest tables or move less important columns to a second table, shorten displayed artifact paths using stable aliases, reduce avoidable hyphenation, and widen the line-number field to preserve all digits.
issues.verification_test: Render all 20 pages and inspect them at 100% zoom and on a letter-size print preview. Every label and table cell should be readable without magnification, no path should collide or overflow, and every displayed line number should be unique and complete.

ethics_concerns: No specific ethics concern is apparent from the PDF. The work uses an existing PG-19 training split for systems evaluation and does not report human-subject research or deployment-quality claims. The stated broader risk that efficiency may increase deployment scale is adequate for the paper's bounded scope.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A clean, independently replayable instantiation on a second runtime or hybrid model that passes the same semantic oracle and ownership predicates would materially strengthen the claimed generality.
A complete source-identity closure showing that every imported executable byte for the primary run is bound to the frozen aggregate would remove the main provenance ambiguity.
A clearer main-text cohort and claim map, combined with consistent equivalence terminology and readable figures, would make the existing contribution substantially easier to evaluate.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Evidence that files omitted from terminal code closure could affect imported execution semantics would undermine the frozen-identity target and central audit result.
A blind replay failure for any registered cross-cell digest, storage-disjointness predicate, selected numerical oracle, or matched-clean control would materially reduce soundness.
Discovery that the negative Transformers result arises from a mismatched input, mask, position, or scale contract rather than runtime behavior would weaken the stated portability boundary.
review_limitations: PDF-only review: I read and visually inspected all 20 pages but did not access the accompanying artifact, raw receipts, code, data, source files, or machine-readable evidence, so replayability and numerical provenance cannot be independently verified.
